speaker: Jessica Guzman
words: Okay Hello good day, this interview is being conducted for the Oral History project, Realities of Undocumented immigrants, the interviewer is Jessica Guzman,

speaker: JG
words: The narrator is using the alias Maria Avila. The interview is taking place over a call on the first of April, 2021.

speaker: JG
words: Maria Avila is someone who has self-identified as currently or having been undocummented, she will be speaking on her experiences in Nevada.

speaker: JG
words: She will also be speaking on her experiences of integration in Nevada, her needs for resources, and worries like: being or having been

speaker: JG
words: undocumented in Nevada, like healthcare, personal challenges of arriving to Nevada and being [un]documented, and a little about the immigration status.

speaker: JG
words: So, could you indicate the name you will be utilizing for this interview.

speaker: Maria Avila
words: Yes, Maria Avila.

speaker: JG
words: Thank you. Maria, in the first place, we spoke to you about the information of the project... what it is about, what we

speaker: JG
words: are looking for, all of that, and we explained that your participation in this project is voluntary. Do you confirm that you accept to participate?

speaker: MA
words: Yes, I am in agreement.

speaker: JG
words: Very well, let's start. So, MA, in an earlier conversation that I had with you, you mentioned that you came from México to

speaker: JG
words: the United States, when you were just around 20 years old; would you tell me a little more about your life in México,

speaker: JG
words: and why you came here to Nevada? Please tell me as much or as little as you feel comfortable.

speaker: MA
words: Yes, well I came with my partner here but, Well it was totally different to life in Mexico, it was huge change.

speaker: JG
words: Yes, I can imagine. You, I think you told me that you are from Tacambaro?

speaker: MA
words: Yes from Tacámbaro, Michoacán.

speaker: JG
words: Yes and when you remember that town, what do you remember most?

speaker: MA
words: Well, overall my family, my family is what I miss most because well, One leaves everything over there. Yes the customs, traditions, everything, everything.

speaker: MA
words: One comes, well here and life is completely different, everything, everything changes. life is completely different, everything, everything changes.

speaker: JG
words: Yes, I imagine it is something very difficult, leaving your family in another country, so, how did you feel when you came to

speaker: JG
words: Nevada and left behind your family and your country of origin?

speaker: MA
words: Well very sad, very- I felt very alone, everything, well I have no family here so I did encounter, like depression, I was very- because of everything, the change that I did.

speaker: JG
words: Yes, I agree. And when you were, well preparing to come here to Nevada, did you have to make something like a plan,

speaker: JG
words: or did you have cost that you needed to come here?

speaker: MA
words: Yes, well the person with whom I came, well they are not my partner anymore but he had a place where we could

speaker: MA
words: stay and he was the one who paid for, well, the trip and everything that needed to be paid.

speaker: MA
words: But it was very difficult to start from the bottom, everything again.

speaker: JG
words: Yes I can imagine that it is something very difficult just leaving everything and having to come to a new country.

speaker: MA
words: Yes, yes it is very difficult, and well, one we were...

speaker: MA
words: I had my children, and then one has to try to get accustomed here to life here in Nevada, here in the United Sates practically.

speaker: MA
words: But yeah, one always has fear, yes because of one's status, one does not have. One goes out on the streets with fear.

speaker: JG
words: So now that, I know you are describing alot, what was a big change when you came for the first time to Nevada?

speaker: JG
words: What did you have trouble adjusting to here? Did you see things, how can I say, did you see cultural differences here in

speaker: JG
words: Nevada, and did you struggle adapting to those cultural differences here?

speaker: MA
words: Yes, about everything. Well, different customs, and overall. Well, the food, that is even though one does try to make it like in one's country.

speaker: MA
words: But yeah, it is not always, well [it does not always] come out good and that's with everything. And, but yes, it is difficult.

speaker: JG
words: And also considering other cultural differences here, like living in Nevada for almost- since 2005, am I right?

speaker: JG
words: Have you been able to learn English to integrate more in Nevada?

speaker: MA
words: Well you see, I have not been able to attend, a long time ago I wanted to go to English school but, because of my kids I could not, I have not been able to go.

speaker: MA
words: And I want to- I know a little, I understand a little but not enough. It is not enough and I want to well, go to school but, now with my job, the kids, I do not have that time.

speaker: JG
words: Yes, it is something difficult because, well when someone for example, wants to learn the language and when they can not becasue of

speaker: JG
words: responsibilities, it is difficult to try to do that, yes.

speaker: MA
words: Yes and well, it is needed for everything, it [English] is needed at my place of work, for everything, everything It is needed.

speaker: MA
words: And yes it gives me, it makes me mad yes, because I say "oh no, why can't I learn," why don't I learn.

speaker: MA
words: But yes, I'll tell you one of those is that I have not have time to dedicate.

speaker: MA
words: Where I say I am going to school, I am going to dedicate [time] soley to learn, and not right now I can not.

speaker: JG
words: Yes I understand. So, like learning English can, it is like a challange for you since you have not had that time to

speaker: JG
words: learn, but what other daily challanges do you encounter because of being indocummented her in Nevada?

speaker: MA
words: Well there are many many challenges here, overall, well one goes out on the streets with fear of this insecurity that well, because of what is racism.

speaker: MA
words: Well, and one says like-

speaker: JG
words: And I know you had told me about, that day you explained that you have faced a lot of racism, I know that

speaker: JG
words: when you go to the store they say things, would you like to speak more on that?

speaker: MA
words: Yes well, I understand, as I said, a little English

speaker: MA
words: And, I know that they are calling me a bad word because I understand that, but I have not fought or responded back to those people.

speaker: MA
words: I instead distance myself, and well yes, because I know that as one is here without documentation, well, one has the losing side.

speaker: MA
words: Yes, I have witnessed cases where there are people who look at me like, "Why are you here?" or "Why don't you go to your country?"

speaker: JG
words: Because of what you have encountered, how does that make you feel? Does it make you feel sad, angry or how does it

speaker: JG
words: make you feel when you have to confront that, that type of-

speaker: MA
words: I feel sad and well, it makes me angry but, I do not, I can not do anything, as I said, I instead distance myself and say it's okay.

speaker: MA
words: It's okay and I try to breath and I, almost control myself, right, because, one gets angry and you can say a lot of things.

speaker: MA
words: And many more things can happen, yes well, here, one is always on the losing side, since here, one can not, like now raise their voice or something like that.

speaker: JG
words: Yes, it is something very frustrating and sad, so, when you encounter that, do you also encounter it at the store or when you work or something like that?

speaker: MA
words: Well yes.

speaker: MA
words: Sometimes at work, like, there are people who hold a position higher than mine and they look at you like, that your, like your work does not count.

speaker: MA
words: And that, well, there are people who do, do make you feel that.

speaker: JG
words: Yes, I understand, and I know- oh go on.

speaker: MA
words: And on the streets too.

speaker: MA
words: Sometimes one will be driving and people will give you looks. Those who are next to you, or that one feels when they are like, talking about you.

speaker: MA
words: But yes I am always like, well in my case, like that, with the sense of fear now.

speaker: JG
words: And this, the elections that have passed in the year 2016 and the one that just passed in 2020, do you think that

speaker: JG
words: you have noticed more like, that you have encountered more racisim after these elections that have passed?

speaker: MA
words: Well I think that it is the same, I have not seen many changes because, well as I said no- people always always look at us like we are different, like "why are you here?"

speaker: JG
words: Yes, yes and does that scare you, now that you have said that you have children,

speaker: JG
words: and that worries you regarding taking care of your kids and all of that, right?

speaker: MA
words: Yes, yes well yes, it is what I fear most; in the case that something, that if the police stops me or they ask for my documents.

speaker: MA
words: I have known of cases where the police well, they can report someone to immigration and that's the fear I have. Because my kids, well they were born here.

speaker: MA
words: and I say, God forbid something like that happen.

speaker: JG
words: Yes, of course it is something, something that would make us all scared, going through those things.

speaker: MA
words: Yes, and one lives that way with those thoughts and well yes, it is difficult.

speaker: JG
words: Yes I agree And, do you think, well, in your opinion, if you think that it is more difficult for people to try to live, make a living and earn money if they are undocummented here?

speaker: MA
words: Yes I think it is more difficult.

speaker: JG
words: Oh, go on.

speaker: MA
words: Well overall to work in a good job, well you need to have your documments in order, in check to earn more or less a good salary.

speaker: MA
words: And another thing well that in order to have access to like, health insurance and that also is that, now yes by all means it is difficult for us.

speaker: JG
words: Which resources have you been missing because of being undocummented here in Nevada like, the medical attention, or other things?

speaker: MA
words: Yes well yes, overall the medical care, since one does not count on health insurance and welll yes it is, it is very expensive when one does not have that, a health insurance.

speaker: JG
words: Yes of course.

speaker: MA
words: Yes

speaker: JG
words: Yes go on.

speaker: MA
words: And well yes like I tell you,

speaker: MA
words: It is difficult for one to be here and more so when one does not have that, like support from a family member.

speaker: MA
words: Or someone who says well, do not worry I will take care of the kids that, because in my case I do not have family here, so it makes it much much harder on me.

speaker: JG
words: Yes of course now that you are the only one from your family that is here in the United states.

speaker: JG
words: So I imagine that the, that makes you feel that you are alone.

speaker: MA
words: Yes, yes I would say, it gives me sadness and I say but.

speaker: MA
words: Well the future of my kids is here and for them and well, so they can study and have a career or something. If they can have a better life than I.

speaker: JG
words: Yes of course, of course, and also, I know we already talked a little about not having medical attention, do you think that

speaker: JG
words: there is a type of inequality in the healthcare system towards undocummented people in Nevada?

speaker: MA
words: Oh well, I think that not definitively but, yes when they ask if you have health insurance and they respond: "no, why?"

speaker: MA
words: Or "why don't you get it?" or but, well as I said yes because that, because that part well, and it is a little bit difficult.

speaker: JG
words: Yes of course, so now with, for example, not having many resources for those who are undocummented, if, for example, if you could

speaker: JG
words: speak with one othe people who make laws like the legistlators here in Nevada, if you were able to speak with them and

speaker: JG
words: you could tell them which resources you need and want here in Nevada, what types of resources would you tell the person who makes the laws?

speaker: MA
words: Oh well yes that of having something that we can have, right, health insurance as well, but it is difficult, like more resources as well, more opportunities for us.

speaker: JG
words: Yes of course.

speaker: MA
words: Those of us that do not count on documentation. Yeah.

speaker: JG
words: And speaking more on the now and what has happened this past year with the Covid-19 pandemic, how has, how has the pandemic

speaker: JG
words: impacted you in places like home, work, etc.

speaker: MA
words: Well, you see it has been very difficult for everyone because, I have been without a job as well, and yeah.

speaker: MA
words: Very difficult, I have been behind on rent, and now, going to work and leaving my kids also, no it is very difficult,

speaker: MA
words: And one goes out with fear beacause one thinks what if I bring the virus home.

speaker: MA
words: What if I come in contact with someone who I don't know, has the virus and then I get it, and I come home with the kids.

speaker: MA
words: Thats the fear that, that I always have.

speaker: JG
words: Yes, it is something that many people are thinking now that many go to work and are always thinking that if someone they

speaker: JG
words: work with has it or if they get something like that it is something very- it is a thought that also scares many people.

speaker: MA
words: Yes, yes overall well one goes out to the store or some place and says one does not know, even though you don't

speaker: MA
words: come in contact with those people but either way one always has fear.

speaker: JG
words: Yes, of course. About, also with the information of Covid-19,especially the vaccine, do you think that you have information that you can read

speaker: JG
words: about what is, or what the virus is, something like that, do you think that you have access to this information?

speaker: MA
words: Yes, well I know of the different vaccines that are given and now as a matter of fact I, they are going to schedule an appointment, for my job by their part.

speaker: MA
words: My workplace's part to receive the vaccine, they have not told me when they will give it to me because you see it is by appointment.

speaker: MA
words: But yes, on that side I do have doubts because I do not know if they are going to give me one dose or two, it's what I do not know yet.

speaker: MA
words: And well I am a little scared becasue you see, the reaction depends on the person but we hope that we do not have any [negative] reaction.

speaker: JG
words: I am glad they are going to give you and appointment to get the vaccine and also no, let's hope you do not

speaker: JG
words: have many secondary effects after you receive the vaccine as well.

speaker: MA
words: Yes that is the, a little fear that I have now but well as other people have already gotten it and they have

speaker: MA
words: not commented today, and he tells me "no I did not feel anything" or that, but as I tell you, you see every person is very different.

speaker: JG
words: Yes.

speaker: MA
words: We have different reactions.

speaker: JG
words: And also speaking on the topic of Covid-19, I know a little while back you mentioned that you had problems with paying rent

speaker: JG
words: now that you did not have a job, what other problems did you have during the pandamic, for example: maybe your kids had

speaker: JG
words: to stay at home to take classes online, were there other problems that came out for you now with this pandamic?

speaker: MA
words: Yes well, I had problems with, I was behind with rent since I was not working and yes I was behind on rent.

speaker: MA
words: And I was giving half nothing else, and welll I spoke with the manager at the office and she told me that,

speaker: MA
words: As soon as I was able to catch up on rent, well I should see her because, many times the owners are not accessible

speaker: MA
words: and they wait on the rent even though they tell you they can't, they can not evict you but there are some people

speaker: MA
words: that can do that, and because of that, it is the, the; now it is the worry that I tell you about,

speaker: MA
words: I have been left without a job again and well now to me it is the most important thing, the rent, paying rent.

speaker: JG
words: Yes, yes I imagine.

speaker: MA
words: It is what worries me the most now as I told you now well, thanks to God I have a job.

speaker: MA
words: And now the kids are going to the school one day, and not going the next, but it does give me a little bit of worry

speaker: MA
words: because of what is happening as well but ah, like here.

speaker: MA
words: I do not have much and then the internet goes down and then they can not be in class or their data erases and they can not continue.

speaker: JG
words: Yes, I imagine it is also something frustrating and also something difficult now that sometimes because of internet connection sometimes it is out

speaker: JG
words: of our control because I know sometimes it does not work. very well, so I imagine it causes a big problem for your children when they want to be in class and all of that.

speaker: MA
words: Yes, yes that's the problem well yes, and they are, well, doing it online, all of school.

speaker: MA
words: But now I decided that this year in August, when the new school year started, I told them and they were in agreement as well, that they would go alternatively.

speaker: MA
words: Because the teachers told us that it was not obligated for the kids to go every day, that we could decide if they would be at home doing online,

speaker: MA
words: Or if they wanted to go to school one day by groups, and well, and yeah the kids said yes.

speaker: MA
words: They were in agreement to go and well, yes it helps them because they distract themselves a little and they understand more there at school.

speaker: JG
words: Yes, also how you mentioned that since you do not have family here, no one helps you take care of your children so

speaker: JG
words: I imagine that them going to school at least some days in the week, it helps you with... ah-

speaker: MA
words: Yes, well, I tell you it, does scare me a little because the school where my- my daughter is enrolled, there have been

speaker: MA
words: cases as well, there of Covid-19 that have come up but she, she knows how she needs to be all, all the precautions

speaker: MA
words: and everything but, step-by-step we have learned now to live with this.

speaker: JG
words: Nearly for, well, a year right?

speaker: MA
words: Yes and let's hope that, that now with the vaccine things get better but, well you see now kids can not-

speaker: MA
words: No not yet, they have not said if kids can get the vaccine, maybe later on.

speaker: JG
words: Yes maybe further on but, thinking about everything since you came her to Nevada and also since 2005, and considering what you have

speaker: JG
words: gone through this year of 2020 and all of that, what is for you, your biggest worry with respect to undocumented immigrants here in the United States today?

speaker: MA
words: Well the insecurity is what, well the fear, the fear that one holds, one always has fear of not having that liberty of being like others, like other people.

speaker: JG
words: Yes, of course. And because of that insecurity and that fear I do not know if you have tried but, have you tired to request citizenship or permanent residency?

speaker: MA
words: No, well, I have not submitted any application now well, we have, other people- well the new president that went into office has good proposals.

speaker: MA
words: Hopefully and yes right, if they could- if they could come true but, it appears difficult to... the people-

speaker: JG
words: And before this president came into office for example; did fear or insecurity prevent you from applying for citizenship or permanent residency?

speaker: MA
words: No, well it was also becasue of the fear and that one says well they are going to know where I live and everything, they are going to have all of my information.

speaker: MA
words: Yes, it is becasue of fear.

words: Okay Maria, these are all the questions I have for you, thank you for taking the time to do this interview with me.
